task: Each time the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move. If you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), hard RespondedExistence(at_exit, holding_box)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the clause RespondedExistence(at_exit, holding_box) is the wrong template for 'If you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box.' That wording is the task's 'if you reach a, you must hold c' pattern, which calls for Response(at_exit, holding_box) alone: at_exit holds on the last step, so a Response forces holding_box on that same step, exactly 'carrying the box' at the exit. A RespondedExistence lets holding_box happen before or after, and since the episode ends at the exit only 'before' is possible: an agent that picks the box up once, drops it, and reaches the exit empty-handed satisfies the clause while breaking the task. The compiled machine confirms the weakening (the exit transition pays only when paired with other failures instead of failing on an empty-handed exit by itself). Replace RespondedExistence(at_exit, holding_box) with the hard Response(at_exit, holding_box) and keep the hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), which correctly captures 'pick it up again on your very next move'.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box), hard Response(at_exit, holding_box)
calls.feedback: NO CHANGES NEEDED: ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) hard captures 'each time the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move' (the very-next-step wording, and a fall always empties the hands, so holding_box on the next step is exactly picking it up again). Response(at_exit, holding_box) hard alone captures 'if you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box': at_exit is only the condition of an 'if', so no Existence(at_exit) is due, and since at_exit holds only on the final step the response closes exactly when the box is in hand at the exit. Both clauses are hard as worded, all propositions are declared, the empty FINAL_STATES with the rule-only warning is valid because nothing is commanded unconditionally, and the machine's pending and rejecting states match the two rules.
